summary: Santa Fe National Forest lookout built in 1951 with a cinder-block L-4 cab; staffed into the 1980s and demolished in 1993 or 1994.

facts.design: 14 by 14 ft modified L-4 ground house of cinder block (register: stuccoed cinderblocks)
facts.status_note: Demolished in 1993 or 1994, according to the Forest history.

visit.trail_note: Unpaved road of about 3.1 miles from State Highway 565 (31 Miles Road), not plowed in winter; the road guide suggests parking about a quarter mile from the peak and hiking the rest unless the vehicle is rugged.

events.note: Built under a 1951 cooperative agreement among the Forest, the SCS and the Indian Service; 14 by 14 ft L-4 ground house
Apollinario (Paul) Trujillo staffed the lookout from 1962 to 1975, with his wife Adelires as relief
Regularly staffed through 1984; wet summers and Los Alamos detection methods reduced staffing in the late 1980s
Demolished in 1993 or 1994 per the Forest history; the road guide gives the winter of 1993-1994; the register gives only a 1988 to 2015 window
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on August 30, 2015

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives only a range, 1988 to 2015. The Forest history (1993 or 1994) and the road guide (winter of 1993-1994) both date the demolition within that range.

notes_for_editor: Built 1951 and demolition in 1993 or 1994 agree across the Forest history and the road guide; the register gives only a 1988 to 2015 removal window. The register says the storage shed was built with the lookout; the Forest history says it was moved from Puye Lookout. The Forest history quotes are from its Clara Peak section (index pages 79 to 82). No source states an access rule for the summit, so no access level is recorded; the road details come from a road guide, not the land manager. The register's Google Earth imagery is the only description of the site today. Staffing as_of 1993 is the demolition year, not a dated staffing record. No new photos found.
